The model already has a matching pattern to fix this with -- givens.malloy's SINCE date given -- but nothing analogous exists for a named season window.

probes.query: get_context target_type=view search_text='top customer by spend'; target_type=dimension search_text='customer full name'
probes.result: top_customers view returned at relevance 0.86 with correct code (group_by: customers.full_name, customer_id); full_name dimension returned with no description/doc field at all, unlike customer_id which inherits the source-level 'keyed by customer_id' doc

reasoning: Walking the ladder: dataset is not the cause -- the golden is verified and I independently reproduced $8,817.56 for id 884. agent-call is not the cause for the required entities -- the agent's single get_context call explicitly targeted 'customer name' and 'total spend / revenue' and both required entities (total_sales, customer_id) came back, customer_id at top relevance. get_context/model and get_context/retrieval are ruled out on the same basis: nothing needed was absent, undocumented, or buried -- both required fields were near the top of a single call's results. That leaves construction: sufficient context arrived (customer_id was in hand) and the agent still wrote group_by: customers.full_name alone, discarding the id. This is WRONG-PICK. On owner: full_name carries no documentation anywhere distinguishing it from customer_id as an unsafe grouping key -- the only signal is the source-level 'keyed by customer_id' doc, which doesn't say names collide. Since the docs do not distinguish the two fields's safety for this purpose, owner is model, not agent-skill, per the WRONG-PICK owner rule. A secondary, non-primary factor: the agent never issued a view-type get_context target and never invoked malloy-analysis, so it never found the model's own top_customers view, which already encodes the correct pattern and would have sidestepped the trap regardless of documentation. The sibling case storefront-tour-best-customers passed specifically by taking that view path.
diagnosis: customers.full_name has no #(doc) or any documentation warning that customer names are not unique (1,000 customers hold 769 distinct names per RESULTS.md), while customer_id -- present in the very same get_context response -- carries no field-level warning either, only the source-level 'keyed by customer_id' note. Nothing in the model tells an agent grouping by name alone will silently merge distinct people. The model's own top_customers view already encodes the fix (group_by: customers.full_name, customer_id together) but nothing on customers or full_name points an agent who skips the view toward that convention.
sharedWith: any question ranking or identifying an individual customer by name ('biggest customer', 'top customer', 'which customer') where the agent doesn't reach for the top_customers view -- storefront-tour-best-customers shows the same trap avoided only by that route, not by documentation.

reasoning: The required entity never appeared in any call. Call 1 was unscoped at package level with on-target phrasing for all three needed concepts -- the broadest possible ask -- and returned 0 results; a verbatim replay of that same call returned it fine, at a rank statistically tied with its overview sibling. That rules out agent-call (the ask was right) and get_context/model (docs and labels retrieve fine on replay); it lands on get_context/retrieval as a call-level miss rather than a ranking defect, since nothing came back at all rather than something ranked low. Calls 2-4 were correctly scoped to source:overview once the agent had a working lead, so their inability to surface an order_items-namespaced id is expected, not a fault. The answer came out right because overview is a pure additive extension of order_items with total_sales untouched, so the two entity ids denote the same computation -- inheritance, not a rebuild or independent sibling.
diagnosis: The package-scoped, on-target first get_context call in this run returned 0 results across all three targets where an identical replay returned a full ranked list (order_items:total_sales and overview:total_sales nearly tied at ~0.74-0.75). The agent recovered via a directly-named view and never revisited order_items, so it answered through overview's total_sales -- inherited unchanged from order_items via `extend` in dashboards/overview.malloy -- which is correct today only because the dashboard never shadows that measure.
sharedWith: any case whose first get_context call in a session returns empty against a package that should have results; also any case where a golden anchors entity ids to a base source while an extend-only dashboard source exposes the identical field under a second name
